subject: poor Bayesian p values in N Mixture models run through R/JAGS

messages.author: 7cae77e58c6f814b
messages.subject: poor Bayesian p values in N Mixture models run through R/JAGS
parts:
Hello All:

I am getting quite poor GOF test results (Bayesian p values) (p = 0.005) in N Mixture models run through R/JAGS.  I have run the model both with a Poisson as well as a negative binomial distribution, without covariates, in the abundance portion of the model.  The data are sparse (lots of zeros) on a fish species collected at 24 sites over 28 occasions.

Can anybody suggest a possible recourse given poor goodness of fit?  My goal is to get abundance across sites, from this count data, hence my interest in sticking with the N mixture family of models.

Thanks, Paul Rudershausen

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] poor Bayesian p values in N Mixture models run through R/JAGS
parts:
hi Paul,

 Beyond the obvious suggestion of "try additional models" (ZIP, more covariates, quadratic effects, splines...) you can also take the approach described on p. 277 of the AHM book of living with the overdispersion but adjust the SE's to account for it analogous to the c-hat usage in AIC based model selection. This is an idea Marc and Michael  wrote about in their BPA book and we've used it throughout the AHM book.

regards
andy

Hi Paul,
My colleagues and I have had some great luck extending N-mixture model linear predictors with overdispersion random effects and a ZIP abundance component, albeit with a large data set, and fisheries application to boot! Manuscript submission days away, perhaps we can help you out with some BUGS coding. The zeros trick is magic for these models in Bayesian applications with Bugs or Jags
Nick
